title: Missing Brute Force Protection on Login Endpoint
description: The login endpoint does not implement any rate limiting or brute force protection mechanisms. Attackers can perform unlimited login attempts without any delays, IP-based blocking, or account lockouts. Testing shows that rapid sequential login requests are accepted without any throttling or temporary account lockout. This allows attackers to perform dictionary attacks or credential stuffing attacks against user accounts with no restrictions.
impact: An attacker can perform brute force attacks to guess user passwords without any restrictions. With tools like Hydra or custom scripts, an attacker can attempt thousands of password combinations against known usernames. The lack of rate limiting makes automated credential stuffing attacks highly feasible, potentially compromising multiple user accounts. This could lead to unauthorized account access, data breaches, and compromise of sensitive user information.
evidence:
POC executed 5 rapid sequential login attempts with incorrect credentials. All requests completed successfully:

Request 1: HTTP 200 (18ms)
Request 2: HTTP 200 (11ms)
Request 3: HTTP 200 (11ms)
Request 4: HTTP 200 (14ms)
Request 5: HTTP 200 (13ms)

No HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) responses were received. No delays or exponential backoff were applied between requests. Response times remained consistent, confirming the absence of any rate limiting mechanism. Account was not locked after multiple failed attempts.
remediation:
1. Implement rate limiting on the login endpoint (e.g., 5 attempts per minute per IP address) using middleware or application-level controls
2. Add account lockout after failed attempts (e.g., lock account after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes)
3. Implement exponential backoff delays between failed attempts to slow down automated attacks
4. Log all failed login attempts for security monitoring and alerting
5. Implement CAPTCHA challenges after multiple failed attempts (e.g., after 3 failures)
6. Implement IP-based blocking for repeated failed attempts from the same IP address
7. Consider using rate limiting libraries such as Flask-Limiter (Flask), express-rate-limit (Node.js), or similar middleware for your framework
8. Monitor and alert on suspicious login patterns (multiple failed attempts from different IPs, etc.)
references: OWASP Top 10 2021 - A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures, CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames, CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
toolCallDescription: Document the brute force protection vulnerability with confirmed POC
